## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Abhisamayakathā* ("Discussion of Realization") is a treatise in the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 3.3) of the Khuddaka Nikāya. In this section, *abhisamaya* (rendered by Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli as "convergence") is analyzed in relation to spiritual practice, stating, for example, that "the convergence of seeing is right view" (*dassana-abhisamayo sammā-diṭṭhi*) [Gethin 2001]. This formulation forms part of an analytical scheme that seeks to demonstrate the underlying unity and mutual integration of various doctrinal sets, such as the faculties (*indriya*) and path factors [Gethin 2001].

 According to DharmaNexus, the *Abhisamayakathā* exhibits extensive Pali-internal text reuse, sharing 646 passages with 35 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal relationships occur within the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* itself—notably with the *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1), *Virāgakathā* (Ps 2.5), *Maggakathā* (Ps 1.9), and *Ānāpānassatikathā* (Ps 1.3)—as well as with the *Kathāvatthu* (*Kilesajahanakathā*, Kv 19.1), the post-canonical *Visuddhimagga*, and the commentarial tradition (*Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments are generated by DharmaNexus with Sanskrit texts such as the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, as well as Tibetan translations of the *Prasannapadā*, though these computational matches are not established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
